# `engine-authoring-schema.json`

The last thing the bridge's `engine-schema` verb ever printed: `Paradise.Export`'s thirteen
authored components, as the engine published them at schema version 3.

**It is a snapshot of something that no longer exists.** Since contract v6 the engine declares no
authored components at all — every record moved to the games that use them — so there is nothing
left to generate this from. The verb was removed with the constant it read.

## Why keep it

Two integration tests exercise the addon's authored-component machinery: enabling a component,
filling its host-object references, reading its fields back off a panel. That machinery is
schema-driven, so the tests need *a* schema, and a real project's comes from its game's launcher.
These tests have no game.

So this file stands in for one. It is a fixture in the ordinary sense — a plausible input, checked
in so the test is self-contained — and it happens to have been generated by the real engine rather
than written by hand, which is the only reason it is worth keeping rather than replacing with
something shorter.

## What it is NOT

Not a vendored engine schema, and the distinction matters because this repo used to have one of
those and it was a hazard. The addon merged its own copy underneath a game's dump, first-wins, so
a copy that had drifted would have won against the truth. Nothing loads this file at runtime; only
tests read it, by path, and the addon's own schema resolution never looks here.

Do not "refresh" it against a current engine. There is nothing to refresh it from, and if a future
engine started publishing components again, that would be a contract change worth its own
decision rather than a fixture update.
